faq_slots.question: How soon can you start?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: start_time] only, as given. A one off job with a date (a conservatory before a party, a shopfront before an opening) only as start_time allows; never a same day or a next day claim unless [CV: same_day_available] is yes.

faq_slots.question: How often should windows be cleaned?
faq_slots.answer_brief: What decides it, in plain words: what settles on the glass and the frames between visits (traffic film by a main road, sap and pollen under trees in spring, salt near the coast, bird marks), how the house faces and how the household wants it kept. The trade facts round interval row found no standard gap, so no number is ever given as the usual: a frequency only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]; otherwise say the pattern is agreed with you and nothing more. Never promise a schedule.

faq_slots.question: Why do my windows look streaky or spotty soon after they've been cleaned?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different causes in plain words, from the trade facts what goes wrong and facts rows: tap water drying on the glass and leaving its minerals behind as white spots; dirt held in the frames, the sills and the seals that the next shower carries down over the pane; grit rubbed across the glass by a cloth or a blade, which marks rather than cleans. Then what the local factor adds (hard water, a main road, trees, the sea), then what a proper clean does about each: water stripped of its minerals, the frames washed with the glass, nothing abrasive on the pane. Blame the method, never the customer's effort. Never promise the glass stays clean after rain (the rain after cleaning row).

faq_slots.question: Do you use ladders?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts ladder and pole rows only: ladders are not banned in this trade and their use follows an assessment of the job; most upstairs windows are done from ground level by pole where the window can be seen and reached safely, and a ladder is kept for short jobs a pole cannot do, secured where it can be. Written as how good window cleaning is done; this client's own kit only from [CV: materials_methods]. Never a reach figure, never a time limit on a ladder, never anything that reads as the customer going up themselves, never a conservatory roof walked on.

faq_slots.question: Can you clean the windows if I'm not in?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: access_handling] and the confirmed practices only (customer_need_not_be_home): whether the customer needs to be in, the side gate, keys for a commercial site. When nothing is on file, say the arrangements for getting in are agreed before the first visit and nothing more. A note or a message when no one was home, payment by card or app, only from the confirmed ticks. Never a key policy, vetting or a DBS check stated as fact unless the client values confirm it.

faq_slots.question: Will you need to walk on the conservatory roof or the solar panels?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Used only when the client's services list carries the conservatory cleaning or solar panel cleaning page. No: from the trade facts conservatory roof access and walking on panels rows, a glass or polycarbonate roof is never treated as something to stand on and a panel is never walked on, because pressure on the cells can crack them. The roof or the array is reached from the ground or from assessed access, a soft brush and purified water doing the work (the stages rows), with the gentler method polycarbonate and self cleaning glass ask for. Never a figure, never a warranty claim, never a promise about what the panels will generate.

Nothing about when the job can start unless [CV: start_time] is set. Never a number unless [CV: typical_jobs] gives one.

A.question: What happens to the dirty water and the debris?
A.answer_brief: From the trade facts stages and the pollution rows only: leaves, moss and silt out of a gutter are collected; wash water from a bin store or cladding is kept out of the surface water drains; a pure water rinse off glass is water stripped of its minerals and nothing added. Whether the debris leaves with the business only from the waste_removal practice and [CV: waste_carrier_registered]; otherwise say it is cleared or left as agreed. Never a product name, never a permit's name.

cards.title: Spots back on the glass after the first shower
cards.brief: Round pages (the Window cleaning category: residential, commercial, sign and canopy): what the customer sees, from the trade facts signs rows in their words (water spots, bird marks, grit on the panes, dirty frames), glass that looks fine for a few days and then marks up in the rain. The one cause this card makes: dirt held in the frames, the sills and the seals, which every shower carries down over the pane (the rain after cleaning row: rinse water stripped of its minerals dries without marks, but later rain still brings down whatever sits above the glass). What a regular visit does about it: the frames and the sills washed with the glass each time, so there is less to run, written as how good window cleaning is done and as this client's practice only where the frames and sills tick is confirmed. On the Exterior cleaning (Pressure Washing Service) or Gutter cleaning category the card reads as what the rain carries down the wall: streaks under a gutter that spills, dark runs down render or cladding (the fascia and cladding signs rows), the same cause, dirt held above washing down. Not tap water drying white: the symptom FAQ owns that. Never a promise the glass stays clean, never a lifestyle line about the view.
cards.mechanism: dirt held in the frames and sills washing down the glass

cards.title: Green creeping over the roof, the frames and the sills
cards.brief: Periodic extras: roof panels gone green or cloudy, grime along the glazing bars, green patches on the roofline, a green film on cladding, the shaded side of a patio dark and slippery, from the conservatory, fascia and cladding signs rows. The one cause this card makes: algae and moss settling wherever a surface stays damp and shaded (under trees, the north side, a roof at a shallow pitch, a sill the sun never reaches). What the visit covers, from the trade facts stages: loose debris comes off first. Then the frames, the roof and the bars are washed by pole, a soft brush and purified water doing the work. Nobody stands on the roof (the conservatory roof access row). Polycarbonate and self cleaning glass get the gentler method their maker asks for (the polycarbonate and self cleaning glass rows), and a pressure wash only where the surface and the job allow it. Say why these are booked once or twice a year rather than on the round: the growth comes back slowly, so round customers add them to a visit when the sign shows. On a round page the card reads as the frames and sills going green on the shaded side between visits, the same cause. No pressure figure, no interval as this client's offer (only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]). Never promise it will not come back.
cards.mechanism: algae and moss settling where a surface stays damp and shaded

cards.title: Upstairs glass nobody gets close to
cards.brief: Round, high level and commercial pages: upper panes noticeably dirtier than the ground floor, marks left above where a pole reached before, staining round glass nobody can get near, dusty upper windows on an office or a shop (the high level and commercial signs rows). The one cause this card makes: windows out of easy reach are cleaned less often, or never, so what lands on them stays and bonds, and bonded grit needs a more careful clean later (the skipped rows). How good work reaches them, from the trade facts stages and facts rows: from the ground with a pole wherever the window can be seen and reached safely, a ladder kept for short jobs a pole cannot do and secured where it can be, and on a commercial building an assessed platform, cradle or rope access chosen by the assessment and never by a set height. Written as how the trade works, never as this client's kit unless [CV: materials_methods] confirms it. Never a reach figure, never a time limit on a ladder, never a line that reads as the customer going up themselves, never a conservatory roof or a flat roof walked on. On the Exterior cleaning or Gutter cleaning category the card reads as the roofline and the gutters out of reach, with a gutter vacuum worked from the ground where the gutter suits it, the same cause.
cards.mechanism: windows out of easy reach cleaned less often, or never

cards.title: A schedule that lapsed
cards.brief: Commercial, sign and bin store pages: the shopfront marked by opening time, fingerprints on the door glass, a sign dulled, a bin store that smells and draws flies between collections (the commercial, sign and bin store signs rows). The one cause this card makes: the gap between visits longer than the build up, so every clean has become a catch up. What a regular visit takes in around trading hours (the front glass, the door, the frames, the sign, with the upper floors on a longer cycle) as what usually happens; visits outside opening hours only from [CV: out_of_hours_available]. A bin store washed and disinfected after the products have been assessed, with the wash water kept out of the surface drains (the bin store stages and the contaminated wash water row), never a product name. On a residential round page the card reads as the first visit after a long gap: a bigger job, because the frames hold what has built up and it runs on to the glass over the first clean or two (say so honestly), and then each visit is shorter. On the Gutter cleaning category the card reads as a gutter overflowing in a downpour, weeds sprouting from it, a downpipe that no longer drains (the gutter signs row). Same cause: the gap since the last clear was longer than the leaves and moss took to fill it. The consequence from the skipped row: a wet wall, soaked brickwork, damp indoors. The manufacturer's guidance (a clear at least once a year, more often under trees) is given as guidance and never as a rule. A frequency as this client's offer only from [CV: visit_frequency_options].
cards.mechanism: the gap between visits longer than the build up

problems.h2: When It's Time for a [SERVICE] Visit

cards.title: The first signs
cards.brief: The things a customer notices first, from the trade facts signs row for this service, in their words: water spots and bird marks, dust on the panes, a green or cloudy roof, panels that have dulled, a gutter that spills in heavy rain, a smell between bin collections. The one cause this card makes: the job left undone. Round pages: what shows between visits. Periodic extras: the sign the customer has watched build for months. Commercial pages: what a customer walking past sees. Then what it leads to if left, from the skipped row: grit that bonds so the next clean has to be gentler, water running down the wall, output that can fall on a soiled panel ('can', no figure). Specific, never alarming, never 'your windows are dirty'.

cards.title: It got worse after a go with the hose
cards.brief: The customer's own attempt, from the trade facts done badly and facts rows: tap water from a hose that dried into white spots, a stiff brush or a blade that scratched the glass, a solvent restorer that marked a uPVC frame, a jet wash across a polycarbonate roof. The one cause this card makes: tap water's minerals and a tool wrong for the surface. Blame the method, never the customer's effort. What the visit does differently: water stripped of its minerals, a soft brush, and the maker's own method for coated glass, polycarbonate and panels (the leaded glass, uPVC and polycarbonate rows). Never a water figure, never a product name unless [CV: materials_methods] gives it. Not frame dirt running down the glass: the category page owns that.
cards.mechanism: tap water's minerals and a tool wrong for the surface

cards.title: A clean that can't put it right
cards.brief: The honest card: misting between the panes, a scratch, etching, a frame gone chalky or yellow. The one cause this card makes: a failed seal, a scratch or an etch, which no clean removes. From the trade facts scratched glass and self cleaning glass rows: a blade or an abrasive on toughened or coated glass marks it, so nothing is scraped; a mark that does not shift is a glazier's job, and the visit tells the customer which is dirt and which is not. Say so plainly: it earns more trust than a promise. Never a promise about the result, never a dig at another trade.
cards.mechanism: a failed seal, a scratch or an etch, not dirt

cards.title: A job you keep putting off
cards.brief: The customer's side: the conservatory roof, the gutters, the upstairs glass, the panels, left because it means a ladder and a wet afternoon. The one cause this card makes: a job that never fits a weekend and should not be done off a householder's ladder. From the trade facts ladder and fragile roof rows: ladder work follows an assessment and a secured ladder, a conservatory roof is never walked on and a panel never stood on; say it as why the job is given to someone with the kit to do it from the ground, never as the reader climbing up. What the visit changes, from the timing cells: gutters once the leaves have come down, the conservatory before the summer it gets used, panels when the soiling and the owner's assessment call for it, the round keeping the frames clean so less runs on to the glass. A frequency only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]; no promise about the result.
cards.mechanism: a job that never fits a weekend

cards.title: How much glass, and how high
cards.brief: The size factor from the trade facts price row: the number of panes and sides, the roof glazing and its bars, the size of the array, the length of the roofline, the glazed area of a frontage. Say it plainly and give no figure, never a height.

cards.title: How heavy the build up is
cards.brief: From the trade facts price row: bonded dirt on glass, heavy growth on a roof, wet debris and blocked downpipes in a gutter, bird fouling and lichen on panels, heavy residue in a bin store. A first visit on something left a while is a bigger job; after that each visit is priced as a visit. Say the business looks before it prices, from [CV: quote_method] only. Nothing priced on time, no hourly rule.

cards.title: Getting to it safely
cards.brief: From the trade facts price row: obstructed access, a busy pavement to keep clear, restricted hours, a platform, cradle or rope access for high glass, roof access controls on a panel job, waste taken off site. Say why each adds time. No figure, never a height.

cards.title: What's done alongside
cards.brief: Work the visit can take on as well, from the sibling service pages and the services list only: the inside glass with the outside, the conservatory roof with the windows, the fascias with the gutters, the panels while the pole is out. Say that each adds to the visit. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.

steps.brief: How to get in touch and what is useful to send first (how many windows and floors, the roof or the gutters, how long since it was last done, photos if they have them). No promise of a reply time unless [CV: response_time] is set.

steps.brief: What the visit will cover and what it costs. The price agreed before the first visit only when the price_agreed_before_work practice is confirmed. Follows [CV: quote_method]; only say the quote is written if quote_method says so. Never restates "free". A frequency only from [CV: visit_frequency_options].

steps.title: We Start on a Date That Suits You
steps.brief: The first visit goes in the diary on a day that suits the customer. A regular pattern following on only when the maintenance_schedule practice is confirmed. Whether the customer needs to be in, the side gate and keys only from [CV: access_handling] and the customer_need_not_be_home practice. Never mention the price or changes to what is covered.

faq_slots.question: How often should [SERVICE_LOWER] be done?
faq_slots.answer_brief: What decides it, from the trade facts timing row, in plain words: what settles on the surface and how fast (traffic film by a road, sap and pollen under trees in spring, salt near the sea, bird fouling on a panel, leaf fall into a gutter) and the setting of the house. The facts pack found no standard gap for a window round, a manufacturer's guidance of a gutter clear at least once a year and more often under trees, and a site specific schedule for panels: give these as guidance, never as a rule or as this client's offer. A frequency as this client's offer only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]; otherwise say the pattern is agreed with you and nothing more. This is the one place the timing is written; a duration only where the row gives one (the rows say it varies).

faq_slots.question: How much does a [SERVICE_LOWER] visit cost in [CITY]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Prices only from [CV: price_list]; otherwise how the price is reached, from [CV: quote_method] only, and that the figure is agreed before the first visit when that practice is confirmed. The four cost cards above already give what moves the price: name one factor at most, never the list again.

faq_slots.question: Are you insured for [SERVICE_LOWER]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for. Never what it pays or who it covers, and never that a broken or cracked pane is covered unless the client values say so (the trade facts broken glass and insurance row).

faq_slots.question: What if something gets damaged during a visit?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the customer does: tell us and we look at it. Then the reasonable care and skill standard every trade works to. No promise to put it right free. Never invent a guarantee or insurance.

faq_slots.question: Do I need to be in for a [SERVICE_LOWER] visit?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: access_handling] and the confirmed practices only (customer_need_not_be_home): whether the customer needs to be in, the side gate, keys or a contact for a commercial site; visits outside opening hours only from [CV: out_of_hours_available]. When nothing is on file, say the arrangements for getting in are agreed before the first visit and nothing more. A note or a message when no one was home only from the confirmed ticks. Never a key policy, vetting or a DBS check stated as fact.

faq_slots.question: What does a [SERVICE_LOWER] visit include?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The What's Included items said as a sentence, in other words: name the work itself (the glass, the frames and the sills; the roof and its bars; the gutter run, the outlets and the downpipes), never 'on this page' or 'listed above'. The inside glass, the frames or an extra only as the services list and the confirmed ticks give them. What a visit does not cover only from the services list, with one sibling service page or the category page linked.

faq_slots.question: Are there rules or standards for [SERVICE_LOWER]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts rule rows only, written as the way the work is usually done, never as homework for the reader: work at height planned so the ground is used where it can be and a ladder kept for short assessed jobs; wash water from a bin store or cladding kept out of the surface drains; a hosepipe ban checked against the water company's own notice rather than assumed either way; a listed building's consent only where cleaning would change its character, since ordinary washing usually needs none; a waste carrier registration where debris is taken away. Plain words with 'usually' or 'in most cases'; what the customer does only where the row says so. Never a standard's number, an Act's name, a cover figure or legal advice. This slot is used only when the service has rule rows.

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked: the cause in the water, the glass or the frames in plain words, what the local factor adds (hard water, a main road, mature trees, salt air, tall or awkward housing), then what this service does about it. One figure at most. Never a claim that the town's homes have dirty windows, never a water hardness the research does not confirm.

cards.title: Tap water that dries white on the glass
cards.brief: Where the town profile confirms hard water: white spots after a go with the hose, scale on the outside of the panes and the sills, the marks a bucket and a cloth leave. The one cause this card makes: the minerals in the town's water left behind as it dries (the trade facts dissolved minerals row). What follows for the work: water stripped of its minerals dries without them, which is why the trade uses purified water through a pole; never a figure for the water, never a hardness the research does not confirm. Where the profile gives soft water or says nothing, the card is instead the one setting the profile does give (salt spray on the coast dulling glass and pitting frames, or traffic film from a main road), one only. Not frame dirt washing down: the category pages own that.
cards.mechanism: the minerals in the town's water left behind as it dries

cards.title: Trees over the street
cards.brief: Sap and pollen on the glass in spring, leaves in the gutters by late autumn, the shaded sills and the conservatory roofs green sooner, where the town profile gives tree lined roads, parks or older estates with mature trees. The one cause this card makes: what the town's trees drop on glass, roofs and gutters through the year. What follows for the work: windows that need the frames doing as well as the glass, gutters booked once the leaves are down (the gutter interval row, as guidance), a roof under a tree that greens quicker than one in the open. Never say the homes are dirty, never a frequency as this client's offer, never name a street as a problem.
cards.mechanism: what the town's trees drop on glass, roofs and gutters

cards.title: Houses a pole suits, and houses it doesn't
cards.brief: Bungalows, three storey townhouses, flats with glass above the shops, terraces with no side access, from the town profile. The one cause this card makes: how high and how reachable the town's windows are. What follows for the work, from the trade facts pole and access rows: upstairs glass done from ground level by pole wherever the window can be seen and reached safely; the back of a terrace reached through the house or a rear alley, with the van parked some way off on the end of a long hose; high glass on a block by an assessed platform, cradle or rope access, chosen by the assessment and never by a set height. Never a reach figure, never a street or an estate named as hard to reach or unsafe, never a line that reads as the customer going up a ladder.
cards.mechanism: how high and how reachable the town's windows are

cards.title: Shopfronts that have to look right by nine
cards.brief: The high street, the business park, the school, the managing agents' blocks, from the town profile. The one cause this card makes: the town's trading hours, with glass that has to be clean by opening time and pavements that are busy by then. What follows for the work: visits timed before the shop opens or after it closes (outside opening hours only from [CV: out_of_hours_available]), passers by kept clear of hoses and poles on the pavement (the highway row, in plain words and never the Act's name), upper glass on a longer cycle than the frontage. Where LINKABLE PAGES has no commercial page in this town, the card is the town's conservatories and extensions (the profile: estates of a certain age) and their roofs going green. Never name a business.
cards.mechanism: the town's trading hours and the frontages they keep

cards.title: Parking a long way from the glass
cards.brief: Terraced streets with permit parking, flats above shops, a long run of hose from wherever the van could stop. Say why that adds time to a visit, from the town profile where it gives the housing and the streets. No figure.

cards.title: Three floors and roof windows
cards.brief: Taller houses, dormers and roof windows, conservatories and extensions the profile gives: more panes and more reach. Say it plainly; no figure, never a height.

cards.title: Windows that haven't been done for a while
cards.brief: The first visit on a home or a shop that has had a long gap is a bigger job than the visits that follow, because the frames hold what the rain then carries down the glass. Say it plainly, from the profile where it gives turnover (new estates, lets, shops changing hands); no figure; not the service pages' first visit card in the same words.

cards.title: Working round the town's hours and pavements
cards.brief: A shop street done before opening, an office out of hours, a school in the holidays, a busy pavement where people have to be kept clear of the kit. Say why a fixed window and a crowded pavement add to the visit, from the profile where it gives the premises. Out of hours work only where [CV: out_of_hours_available] confirms it. No figure.

faq_slots.answer_brief: From the confirmed practices only: whether the customer needs to be in (customer_need_not_be_home), the side gate and keys from [CV: access_handling], how the visit is agreed, out of hours for commercial work only from [CV: out_of_hours_available]. faq_slots.question: Do you clean windows in [TOWN] all year round?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Yes, from the trade facts timing cells: the work runs all year and a visit stops only for high wind, lightning and the days the rinse water would freeze on the paths. Then what the town's seasons put on the glass, from the profile where it gives them: sap and pollen in spring under the trees, leaves in the gutters in autumn, salt after a winter storm on the coast. Say why the timing changes the job; never fall back on 'our busy season'. No dates, no promise of a slot.
